packageRules.description: GitHub Actions touch CI credentials directly — longer cooldown, and always a human merge regardless of how clean the diff looks. Matches the asymmetry docker-ansible's own renovate.json uses.

Docker base-image digest bumps: low blast radius (a rebuild, not a permission change) and this repo's own OS-patch-at-build-time control already assumes fresh bases — automerge once CI is green and the cooldown has passed.
Python/JS dependency patch bumps: automerge after cooldown + green CI, same reasoning as Docker digests above.
Minor/major dependency bumps get a human look — a range widen or a real API change is not the same risk class as a patch.

Go modules (ADR 0011): the relay's only third-party code is the OpenTelemetry SDK and the Prometheus client. A week's cooldown and always a human merge, whatever the update type, because a bump moves relay/go.mod and with it the coverage floor's gomod= hash. postUpdateOptions keeps go.sum tidy for scripts/check_go_deps.sh.
The OpenTelemetry Go modules release together and depend on each other's exact versions; a split bump does not build. One update for all of them.
govulncheck, run by go-tests.yml at the version in its GOVULNCHECK_VERSION env (ADR 0011). Same cooldown as the Go modules.

customManagers.description: go-tests.yml's govulncheck job pins the tool by version in an env value; `go run pkg@version` verifies it against the Go checksum database.
